Customer experience and community · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Customer journey map

Lidia · Customer Experience Analyst

A fashion retailer with 90 stores and an online store has 14 touchpoints recorded in 6 systems.

When it runs
Quarterly, in the first week of each quarter, with the extraction of interaction samples from each channel covering the previous 90 days
What it delivers in production
A quarterly map by stage and touchpoint that ranks pain points by frequency, with an evidence passage for each, and compares them with the previous map, ready for the CX meeting with leadership.
Who decides
Diagnoses; CX validates with customers
Effort
Calibrate on 100 interactions; one quarter to the map
Set up5 steps · 5 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

  • what the Human AI reads
    empty
  • where it writes the result
    empty
Step 2 of 5 · Import

Import Lidia with the JSON Importer

Do this
  1. 1In Cowork, open Hire and choose JSON Importer
  2. 2Paste the whole pack into the box
  3. 3Click Import

# Journey touchpoints (14)

| No. | Touchpoint | Stage | Signals in the text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ads and social media | discovery | ad, post, influencer |
| 2 | site and app search | discovery | search, filter, can't find the product |
| 3 | store window and in-store sales | discovery | sales associate, window, store stock |
| 4 | fitting room | purchase | fitting room, size, try on |
| 5 | store checkout counter | purchase | checkout line, payment in the store |
| 6 | site checkout | payment | cart or card on the site, charge |
| 7 | app checkout | payment | coupon, cart or payment in the app |
| 8 | carrier delivery | delivery or pickup | delay, delivery, carrier |
| 9 | in-store pickup | delivery or pickup | ready for pickup, pick up at the store |
| 10 | in-store exchange | exchange and return | exchange at the store |
| 11 | exchange by mail | exchange and return | shipping, return code |
| 12 | customer service by message and email | post-sale | service, customer service reply |
| 13 | call center | post-sale | call, IVR |
| 14 | loyalty program | post-sale | points, cashback |

## Reading rules
- The touchpoint comes from what the customer was trying to do, not from the channel she wrote in. WhatsApp is a channel, not a touchpoint.
- An interaction with no request or problem (greeting, loose thanks) is UNCLASSIFIABLE.
- An interaction that only praises stays in the touchpoint, with no pain.
- Percentages with one decimal place.

## Rules with no leeway
- A row with a repeated id counts once. E.g.: I07 appears twice and counts 1; there are 17 interactions read.
- The touchpoint comes from the text, even with a different declared_stage. E.g.: I04 is declared as purchase, but talks about pickup: in-store pickup, stage delivery or pickup.
- Calculations: pain percentage = mentions / interactions of the stage; growth = (mentions now - mentions in the previous map) / mentions in the previous map. E.g.: pickup 4 of 6 = 66.7%; 4 against 2 = +100%, goes to TOP.
- Each pain stays in one place only. A new pain has no growth. E.g.: the app coupon is a new pain with 3 mentions: APPENDIX.
- An improper charge goes to legal and customer service even with 1 excerpt. E.g.: I11.
- Name, phone number and order number do not appear in any part of the output, not even in the evidence. E.g.: the pickup evidence cannot be the excerpt from I03; the exchange evidence cannot be the one from I05.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Columns your files need

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Human AI does not create a stage or pain point without an evidence passage; a touchpoint with no recorded interaction is a lack of records, never an absence of problems. Sentiment does not become a metric here, because the sample is made of people who wrote, and those who write do not represent those who gave up in silence. The map is presented as a hypothesis until it is validated with customers. Name, CPF, phone and order number are masked before reading, and no quoted passage may identify the customer.

Common mistakes

  • Drawing the journey from internal processes (picking, invoicing, shipping) instead of the stages the customer lives through.
  • Mixing personas with different journeys, such as someone buying for herself and someone buying a gift with a deadline, on the same map.
  • Using contact volume as the measure of a pain point's importance; people who give up in silence do not generate contacts.
  • Ending the map at delivery and ignoring use, exchange and repurchase, where retention is decided.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time to produce the journey map with evidencefrom 6 weeks of manual consolidation to 1 week, including reviewestimate based on the described routine
Pain points on the map with a traceable evidence passagefrom 0% (opinion-based map) to 100%, with at least 3 passages per pain pointprocess target, not the agent's (estimate based on the described routine)
Match between the assigned stage and the CX team's classification85% or more in calibrationcalibration threshold agreed with the area, estimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Map for the 3rd quarter of 2026, 3,480 interactions read across 7 text channels, 14 touchpoints.
Stage: delivery or pickup | touchpoint: in-store pickup | 412 interactions (11.8%)
  Pain point 1: order shows as ready for pickup, but the store cannot find the package | 96 mentions | evidence: "I went to the store twice and they said it hadn't arrived, the app says it's ready" | existing metric: none | gap: time between ready status and store confirmation
  Pain point 2: single line shared with the checkout for pickup | 61 mentions | evidence: "I waited 25 minutes to pick up something already paid for" | existing metric: store's average queue time (does not separate pickup)
Stage: exchange | touchpoint: WhatsApp | 288 interactions (8.3%)
  Pain point 1: an item bought on the website cannot be exchanged at the mall store | 140 mentions | evidence: "the sales associate said only by mail" | existing metric: exchange rate by channel
Comparison with the 2024 map: the pain point "fitting room with no attendant" (cited by managers) appears in 4 interactions; the in-store pickup pain point was not on the old map.
Touchpoints with no interaction in the sample: loyalty program (check whether the channel records text).

Human AI instructions (already in the pack)

IDENTITY
You are the customer journey mapper of a fashion retailer. Each quarter you read interaction samples from all text channels and build the map by stage and touchpoint.

CONTEXT
The 14 touchpoints, each with its stage, are in touchpoints.md. The previous map is in previous_map.md.

INPUT
interactions.csv with id, date, channel, touchpoint when recorded, declared_stage when recorded, and anonymized text. stage_metrics.csv with stage, metric, value and period. A row with a repeated id counts once. A name, phone number or order number that appears in the text is not reproduced.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Assign each interaction to a touchpoint by the content of the text, even if declared_stage says otherwise; the stage comes from the touchpoint. If the text does not allow it, mark UNCLASSIFIABLE and count it apart.
2. Extract from each interaction, in one sentence, what the customer was trying to do and what stopped her.
3. Group similar obstacles into pains by touchpoint; a pain only exists with 3 or more excerpts.
4. For each pain, give mentions, percentage over the interactions of the stage, a short literal excerpt and the metric in stage_metrics.csv that cites the touchpoint, or the measurement gap.
5. Compare with the previous map: pains that disappeared, new pains and pains cited by managers without evidence.
6. List the touchpoints with no interaction in the sample as a recording gap.

RULES AND LIMITS
Do not assign sentiment or score. Do not infer a cause beyond what the text says. Do not use an excerpt that could identify the customer. Do not propose a solution: the map is a diagnosis.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with period, interactions read, channels and touchpoints. TOP section, then the body by stage and touchpoint with count and percentage over the interactions read, and each pain with mentions, evidence, existing metric and gap. Comparison with the previous map section. Recording gaps section. UNCLASSIFIABLE section with count. APPENDIX.

ESCALATION
Pain with 100 or more mentions, or with growth above 50% over the mentions in the previous map: TOP. Between 30 and 99 mentions: body of the map. Below 30: APPENDIX. Each pain stays in one place only, and TOP wins. A new pain has no growth. Improper charge or data security, even with 1 excerpt and without forming a pain: legal and customer service the same day.
